top_examples.hook: My coworker stole my lunch for an entire week, then reported me to HR because the last one was too spicy.
top_examples.premise: A coworker secretly steals the narrator's homemade lunches for a week, then reports the narrator to HR after taking a naturally extra-spicy meal.
top_examples.title: She Stole My Lunch, Then Reported Me to HR

top_examples.hook: My grandmother thought she was becoming forgetful. Then the grocery store texted her about salmon she had never received.
top_examples.premise: A woman discovers her cousin has been quietly changing the delivery address on their grandmother's online grocery orders and keeping the expensive items while delivering only basics.
top_examples.title: She Made Grandma Think She Was Forgetful

top_examples.hook: Two weeks before my wedding, the bakery told me I had apparently chosen a cake flavor I can't even eat.
top_examples.premise: A woman discovers the bakery making her wedding cake has secretly replaced her paid premium tasting selections with cheaper flavors for another couple willing to pay a rush fee.
top_examples.title: The Bakery Changed My Wedding Cake Order

top_examples.hook: My streaming account suddenly thought I loved Korean pottery documentaries. Apparently, so did the girl my friend was trying to impress.
top_examples.premise: A man discovers his friend has been using his streaming account's watch history to pretend they share obscure interests with someone they are trying to date.
top_examples.title: My Friend Used My Netflix History to Impress a Date

top_examples.hook: I thought my expensive serum had suddenly stopped working. Then I realized it had also changed color.
top_examples.premise: A woman notices her expensive skincare empties unusually fast and discovers her visiting sister-in-law has been refilling the bottles with cheap lotion while taking the originals home.
top_examples.title: Someone Was Refilling My Skincare Bottle

weak_retention_examples.hook: My contractor installed cheap tiles and sent the ones I paid for to someone else's house.
weak_retention_examples.premise: A homeowner pays for premium imported tiles during a renovation, but the contractor installs cheaper lookalikes and sends the expensive boxes to another project.
weak_retention_examples.title: My Contractor Gave My Tiles to Another Client

weak_retention_examples.hook: He returned my laptop, but it wasn't my laptop.
weak_retention_examples.premise: A man sells a nearly new laptop online, accepts a return after the buyer claims it is defective, then discovers the buyer mailed back an older damaged version of the same model.
weak_retention_examples.title: He Returned a Different Laptop

weak_retention_examples.hook: My coworker became everyone's hero by saving meetings I supposedly forgot. Then IT checked who had cancelled them.
weak_retention_examples.premise: A woman discovers her coworker has been secretly cancelling her client appointments from a shared calendar and then volunteering to rescue the supposedly abandoned meetings.
weak_retention_examples.title: He Kept Saving the Meetings He Cancelled

weak_retention_examples.hook: Tools kept disappearing from my dad's garage, and I thought retirement was making him reckless.
weak_retention_examples.premise: A man thinks his father is irresponsibly giving away family tools after items keep disappearing from the garage, but learns his father has been secretly teaching free weekend repair classes to young adults aging out of foster care.
weak_retention_examples.title: My Dad's Tools Kept Disappearing After He Retired

weak_retention_examples.hook: My building had photos proving I dumped trash beside the bins. Then I noticed one label that should never have been there.
weak_retention_examples.premise: A tenant is blamed for repeatedly leaving trash beside the recycling bins until a package label reveals someone in the building has been moving her garbage to manufacture complaints.
weak_retention_examples.title: My Neighbor Used My Trash to Frame Me

recent_story_cards.conflict: Residents believe the courier introduced the fee because the neighbor presents printed notices with a payment QR code.
recent_story_cards.payoff: My next package went into the cabinet for free.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his neighbor has been collecting delivery parcels for the building and charging residents a fake redelivery fee.
recent_story_cards.title: My Neighbor Charged Me to Collect My Own Package
recent_story_cards.twist: The neighbor volunteered as the building's parcel contact, then created the notices herself to monetize pickups.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The owner publicly confronts him while staff threaten to cancel his membership.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The locker log did the rest.
recent_story_cards.premise: A gym member is accused of stealing another man's expensive lifting belt after staff find it inside his locker.
recent_story_cards.title: They Found His Stolen Belt in My Locker
recent_story_cards.twist: Locker-access records show the accuser opened the narrator's locker himself to plant the belt after losing an argument over equipment.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Guests think the bride introduced a surprise transport fee and start complaining days before the wedding.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The shuttle was free, exactly as promised.
recent_story_cards.premise: A bride discovers her cousin has been secretly charging relatives for seats on a wedding shuttle the bride already paid for.
recent_story_cards.title: My Cousin Charged Guests for My Free Wedding Shuttle
recent_story_cards.twist: The cousin created a fake payment list to recover money she had lost after booking herself a nonrefundable hotel upgrade.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The brother says he charged only people who requested extra portions and deserves compensation for doing the grilling.
recent_story_cards.payoff: We objected to him opening a restaurant inside someone else's gift.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his brother has been secretly charging relatives for portions of a family barbecue even though their parents paid for all the food.
recent_story_cards.title: My Brother Secretly Charged Everyone at Our Family Barbecue
recent_story_cards.twist: The payment list includes their grandmother, who had already contributed money directly to their parents for the groceries.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Residents keep losing the visitor space while the neighbor insists the booking app must be malfunctioning.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The invisible car finally got towed without ever existing.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man learns his neighbor has been reserving the apartment building's only visitor parking space with a fake car plate whenever her boyfriend plans to visit.
recent_story_cards.title: The Same Invisible Car Booked Our Parking Every Weekend
recent_story_cards.twist: The fake plate belongs to a car her boyfriend sold months ago, and building logs show she has been making duplicate reservations under two units.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The cousin insists it was an emergency because her daughter's cake order had fallen through, while the narrator arrives to an empty pickup counter for her mother's milestone birthday.
recent_story_cards.payoff: She borrowed a cake and returned a reason not to trust her.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers her cousin secretly changed the bakery pickup name on a prepaid birthday cake and collected it for another party.
recent_story_cards.title: My Cousin Collected Mom's Birthday Cake Before I Did
recent_story_cards.twist: The cousin planned to replace the cake later, but photos reveal she served the customized cake with the narrator's mother's name scraped off.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Several acquaintances demand refunds from the narrator because the screenshots show his name and original booking confirmation.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He wasn't selling tickets. He was selling a future he couldn't afford.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man finds out his friend has been using screenshots of his sold-out concert tickets to convince people he can source extra seats for a fee.
recent_story_cards.title: People Wanted Refunds for Tickets I Never Sold
recent_story_cards.twist: The friend never had extra tickets at all; he was collecting deposits and hoping resale prices would fall before the concert.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Her manager praises the coworker for teamwork while questioning why her response times suddenly collapsed.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He built his teamwork award out of my workload.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers her coworker has been quietly forwarding difficult customer emails to her queue, then volunteering to help when she falls behind.
recent_story_cards.title: He Kept Rescuing Me From Work He Secretly Sent Me
recent_story_cards.twist: The forwarding rule was created from the coworker's account, but he claims he only did it because management was comparing their numbers and he was afraid of being cut.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Buyers believe valuable cards from the narrator's collection can appear in the packs, while the friend says the photos were only examples of what collectors might get.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He didn't borrow my cards to photograph them. He borrowed their value.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his friend has been borrowing his Pokémon cards for photos, then using those photos to advertise mystery packs online.
recent_story_cards.title: My Friend Used My Pokémon Cards to Sell Mystery Packs
recent_story_cards.twist: One buyer receives a cheap pack and recognizes the exact rare card in the advertisement from the narrator's social media post.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Their friends repeatedly complain that the narrator is controlling and wasteful because the roommate tells them she refuses to raise the temperature.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Apparently the thermostat was never the problem. The imaginary argument was.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers her roommate has been secretly changing the smart thermostat before guests arrive so everyone blames her for keeping the apartment freezing.
recent_story_cards.title: My Roommate Made Everyone Think I Controlled the Thermostat
recent_story_cards.twist: The roommate is intentionally cooling the apartment before parties because she gets overheated easily, then restoring the setting before the narrator returns.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The roommate promises priority play sessions using the narrator's console and account without permission.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He tried to sell launch day before he even owned launch day.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his roommate has been taking deposits from friends for first-day access to GTA 6 on his console even though the game is not released yet.
recent_story_cards.title: My Roommate Sold GTA 6 Playtime on My Console
recent_story_cards.twist: He has sold overlapping time slots to more people than could possibly play even after release.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Families arrive believing they paid for specific seats, causing an argument before the children's show.
recent_story_cards.payoff: She sold seats the school never owned, then lost the free ones she actually could have taken.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman finds out another parent has been selling reserved front-row seats for a school performance even though seating is officially first-come, first-served.
recent_story_cards.title: A Mom Secretly Sold Front-Row Seats at Our Kids' Show
recent_story_cards.twist: The parent used an old seating diagram from a different event and sold the same front-row positions twice.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Relatives believe the narrator arranged the order because her purchase receipt was used as proof that she had access to a special launch discount.
recent_story_cards.payoff: My receipt proved one purchase, not six imaginary bargains.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman buys an iPhone 18 Pro and discovers her sister has been charging relatives to join a fake family group order for discounted accessories.
recent_story_cards.title: My Sister Invented an iPhone Family Discount Using My Receipt
recent_story_cards.twist: There was no group discount; the sister planned to buy cheaper third-party accessories later and keep the difference.

recent_story_cards.conflict: She says she used the money for genuine household emergencies and always intended to repay it before the trip.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The emergency IOUs needed a conversation. The secret holiday needed a different one.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his girlfriend has been quietly removing cash from their shared holiday jar and replacing it with handwritten IOUs he never noticed.
recent_story_cards.title: Our Holiday Jar Was Full of Secret IOUs
recent_story_cards.twist: Most withdrawals were defensible, but one IOU reveals she paid a deposit for a solo weekend away after telling him they could not afford a couple's getaway.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Other members confront her for hogging equipment, and staff warn her after repeated complaints.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He tried to reserve my reputation because he wanted my treadmill.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers someone at her gym has been moving her water bottle between machines to make it look like she is reserving multiple stations.
recent_story_cards.title: Someone Used My Water Bottle to Make the Gym Hate Me
recent_story_cards.twist: A regular who wanted her usual treadmill admitted moving the bottle after camera footage showed him carrying it around the gym.

recent_story_cards.conflict: He says the points were going to expire anyway, even though she had been saving them for a family celebration.
recent_story_cards.payoff: the real value of loyalty
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers her boyfriend has been using her loyalty points to impress his coworkers with free lunches.
recent_story_cards.title: He Used My Points to Impress His Coworkers
recent_story_cards.twist: The restaurant app shows he redeemed nearly all of them during dates when he claimed he was working through lunch.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The friend denies selling anything and claims the missing tools were never lent to him.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Nobody lent him tools after that
recent_story_cards.premise: A man finds out his friend has been returning borrowed tools to a hardware store for store credit.
recent_story_cards.title: My Friend Returned My Tools for Store Credit
recent_story_cards.twist: A store employee recognizes the narrator's engraved initials on a drill brought in for return.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Several relatives arrive believing the wedding is casual because the bride's sister sent them a fake update.
recent_story_cards.payoff: they deserved to be after being set up
recent_story_cards.premise: A bride learns her sister has been secretly changing the dress code for selected wedding guests.
recent_story_cards.title: My Sister Secretly Changed My Wedding Dress Code
recent_story_cards.twist: The sister targeted only relatives she thought would look better than her in formal photos.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The friend films his failed lifts and jokes about them in their group chat.
recent_story_cards.payoff: a joke ends when both people are laughing
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his gym partner has been secretly adding weight to his bar between sets to embarrass him.
recent_story_cards.title: My Gym Partner Was Sabotaging My Lifts
recent_story_cards.twist: A trainer checks the security footage and catches the friend changing plates whenever the narrator turns away.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The other customer publicly demands he move even though staff say the café does not take table reservations.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The homemade reservation sign disappeared with her
recent_story_cards.premise: A café regular is accused of stealing another customer's reserved table after a handwritten sign appears while he is ordering.
recent_story_cards.title: She Made a Fake Reserved Sign for My Table
recent_story_cards.twist: Security footage shows the customer placing her own reserved sign on his occupied table after he walked to the counter.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The cousin insists every strange expression is just bad timing and accuses her of being vain.
recent_story_cards.payoff: They did all the explaining
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman realizes her cousin has been secretly editing shared holiday photos to make her look worse before posting them.
recent_story_cards.title: My Cousin Edited Every Photo to Make Me Look Bad
recent_story_cards.twist: The shared cloud album contains the untouched originals directly beside the edited copies.

recent_story_cards.conflict: A coworker claims management promised him her window desk and has already moved her belongings into a box.
recent_story_cards.payoff: the desk he tried to steal
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman discovers her office desk has been quietly reassigned while she is on approved leave.
recent_story_cards.title: He Packed My Desk While I Was Away
recent_story_cards.twist: The coworker produced an approval email, but the message was only permission to borrow her monitor for one presentation.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The roommate has been inviting coworkers over for paid homemade dinners and presenting the narrator as hired help.
recent_story_cards.payoff: She paid it without another word
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman catches her roommate charging friends for meals she cooks without telling her.
recent_story_cards.title: My Roommate Was Selling My Cooking
recent_story_cards.twist: One guest asks for a receipt because the roommate promised the meals were part of a side catering business.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The other parent wants her own child to win a classroom display prize and insists the missing labels are the girl's mistake.
recent_story_cards.payoff: everyone knew she hadn't forgotten them
recent_story_cards.premise: A father learns another parent has been moving his daughter's school-project labels so her work looks incomplete.
recent_story_cards.title: She Sabotaged My Daughter's School Project
recent_story_cards.twist: A teacher's time-lapse camera for the project table records the parent switching the labels before judging.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Her neighbor repeatedly reports the mystery car using photos that make it look like it belongs to her visitors.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The car keys did it for me
recent_story_cards.premise: A tenant is blamed for blocking a shared driveway even though she does not own the offending car.
recent_story_cards.title: He Tried to Tow a Car That Wasn't Mine
recent_story_cards.twist: The car belongs to the neighbor's adult son, who parks it near her unit so his father will not know he is visiting his ex nearby.
